rows.task: set-P02 — Add a preset/custom provider; enable canonical OpenAI account provider
rows.existingCli: provider add P [--adapter A --base-url U --api-key ... --default-model M --allow-private-network --force --set-default --sync]; provider edit openai --enabled on

limitations: Without --live this changes local configuration. --sync optionally discovers a local daemon and runs syncModelsToCodex; saved and applied outcomes are separate. No management provider CRUD is performed by this branch.
workflows.condition: omit --live

limitations: Without --live, saves local configuration; --sync reports its actual disposition and needsSync, never fabricated client application. --live cannot be combined with --sync.
Live add reads the target roster and presets. An observed existing row requires --force; POST remains upsert, so the preflight is not atomic create-only protection.
Canonical OpenAI uses the target preset unchanged; transport/auth/model overrides are refused in live add. No local registry fallback when a needed target preset is missing.
Keep real credentials out of argv and agent transcripts; this does not authorize credential capture.
workflows.condition: explicit --live

routes.body: only explicitly supplied provider patch fields

limitations: At least one edit is required; only supplied fields are patched. update is an existing alias. Use provider show only for local state, not as proof of the live write.
Management errors use safe fixed provider diagnostics; catalog failures retain the saved receipt and a nonzero exit.

rows.task: set-P12 — Manage OAuth account roster
rows.existingCli: account list/current/use P I; account alias P I TEXT\|-; account pause/resume P I; account remove P I --yes; all support --json

routes.query: provider=<provider>; quota=1 only with --quota; refresh=1 only with both quota and refresh

limitations: Default listing is observational. --quota can probe provider quotas; --refresh is only acted on together with --quota. A refresh observation is not pending-account validation consent.
This row supplies a provider explicitly and selects only its account family; JSON is {accounts,notes}.
Uses the live route for the configured account family; this does not report the physical native-main profile.
This family passes the exact account/key ID to its live selection route. Codex main/auto aliases do not apply.
This family takes an exact ID; - clears the alias, and aliases are limited to 80 printable characters.

Codex pause unbinds pinned threads and selects a fallback when possible; with no fallback, a paused-but-selected Codex account still receives requests. Anthropic and generic OAuth pause exclude the account from new requests, failover and refresh, and an all-paused pool answers 403. Credentials and health are preserved; already-sent turns are not cancelled.

limitations: This family takes an exact ID and requires --yes. It reads the roster before and after deletion; a failed post-delete read means deletion may already have succeeded.

limitations: Codex resolves IDs and aliases before reserved words; an account actually named auto wins. account clear openai always clears. OAuth and API-key selection pass the ID directly. This does not switch the physical Codex App login.
Only Codex account pools are supported; other families are refused. Sends accountId:null without interpreting auto as an account ID.
Clearing sends accountId:null; explainCodexUseOutcome returns without a post-clear roster or active read.

- clears with an empty string. Codex resolves existing aliases; other families take an ID. Native main cannot be renamed; aliases are at most 80 printable characters. rename is an existing command alias.
Native main removal is refused. Reads the account family before and after deletion; a failed post-delete read means deletion may have succeeded. Only Codex resolves aliases here.
Roster GETs occur both before and after removal; a failed post-delete verification does not imply rollback.
